targetTest: resume blocks the run on one open permission decision naming the action and its parameter summary, and does not call the action again
expected: a killed run with a privileged action that has an action.started and no end: resume opens one permission decision naming it and the run is blocked_on_decision (not delivered); two or three such actions open their decisions in start order; a run with none resumes as before
actual: reconcilePrivilegedSteps is not called by resume, so the resumed run is re-verified and exits 0 as ready_for_review with no decision (the planned assertion that the resume does not deliver the run fails: actual exit code 0); the cases with no interrupted action and the FR-13 case on the four-item run pass in RED
semanticAssessment: The target ran against a real SIGKILLed run (mid-verify) whose ledger held an action.started for x.synthetic without an end; it failed on the planned assertion because the resume path never reads action events, not because of an import, syntax or fixture fault (typecheck clean, the killed run and the privileged start were created in the test body and the resume ran the real supervisor). The empty-edge case and the decision-answer case pass in RED by design: they assert behavior that must not change.
